## Personality

Lynde is an outspoken and farseeing woman who is recognized as an active worker in her church. Known for her sewing skills, she possesses a good, kind, and generous heart that leads her to assist the poor. Despite these charitable qualities, she is also viewed by some as a gossip and not the type of person to whom one would confide deeply personal matters.

## History

Mrs. Lynde offered her assistance when [Matthew](../character/matthew.md) asked for help securing a stylish dress for [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md), and she sewed a brown dress with puffed sleeves for the girl's [Christmas](../codex/places.md#merry-christmas) present. Later in the school year, she visited [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) and commended Anne's growth and character to [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md). She was present to celebrate Anne's success when the entrance exam results were published, showing [Anne](../character/anne.md) tied for first place on the [Island](../codex/places.md#island). After Matthew's sudden death, she joined other neighbors in offering support to the grieving household at [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables). Later, when [Anne](../character/anne.md) began her teaching career, Mrs. Lynde visited [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) and provided unsolicited advice on teaching methods. On another occasion, she walked home with [Anne](../character/anne.md) while discussing church preparations, and she was later mentioned as part of local gossip when [Diana](../character/diana.md) and [Anne](../character/anne.md) discussed local affairs before leaving for [Redmond College](../codex/places.md#redmond-college).

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XVI. Diana Is Invited to Tea with Tragic Results P3](../source/v01-c16.md#nw-v01-c16-p0003), [v1 CHAPTER XVI. ## Quotes

> "I just guess she has done well, and far be it from me to be backward in saying it. You’re a credit to your friends, Anne, that’s what, and we’re all proud of you."
>
> — Lynde — [v1 CHAPTER XXXII. The Pass List Is Out P48](../source/v01-c32.md#nw-v01-c32-p0048)

> "Child, yes, I’m afraid of it. Look at his face. When you’ve seen that look as often as I have you’ll know what it means."
>
> — Lynde — [v1 CHAPTER XXXVII. The Reaper Whose Name Is Death P7](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0007)

> "Well, I wish you would. I guess we’ll have the supper in about a fortnight’s time. Uncle Abe Andrews is prophesying rain and storms for about that time; and that’s a pretty sure sign we’ll have fine weather."
>
> — Lynde — [v2 XIV A Danger Averted P8](../source/v02-c14.md#nw-v02-c14-p0008)

> "It’s because you’re too heedless and impulsive, child, that’s what. You never stop to think—whatever comes into your head to say or do you say or do it without a moment’s reflection."
>
> — Lynde — [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P62](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0062)

> "You must learn to think a little, Anne, that’s what. The proverb you need to go by is ‘Look before you leap’—especially into spare-room beds."
>
> — Lynde — [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P65](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0065)

## Relationships

### [Marilla Cuthbert](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/lynde--marilla-cuthbert.md)

[Marilla Cuthbert](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) and Mrs. Lynde are close neighbors and long-standing acquaintances who offer each other support during times of hardship. They frequently exchange visits and discuss local affairs, including the upbringing and progress of [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) as she grows up in [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea). Their bond is rooted in mutual comfort and shared community ties.

- Friend of — neighbors and close acquaintances who comfort and help each other in tragedy  <sub>[v1 CHAPTER XXX. The Queen’s Class Is Organized P38](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0038), [v1 CHAPTER XXXVII. The Reaper Whose Name Is Death P5](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0005)</sub>

### [Thomas Lynde](../character/thomas-lynde.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/lynde--thomas-lynde.md)

[Thomas Lynde](../character/thomas-lynde.md) is the husband of Mrs. Lynde. They are a married couple who share a home in [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea), living together while Mrs. Lynde actively engages in local community matters.

- Spouse of — married couple  <sub>[v1 CHAPTER XVIII. Anne to the Rescue P1](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0001), [v2 VIII Marilla Adopts Twins P1](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0001), [v2 XXV An Avonlea Scandal P32](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0032)</sub>

### [Emily](../character/emily.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/emily--lynde.md)

[Emily](../character/emily.md) is a friend of Mrs. Lynde. The two struck up a friendship after traveling to [Carmody](../codex/places.md#carmody) together to shop for wallpaper.

[Paul Irving](../character/paul-irving.md) is a young boy in the community whom Mrs. Lynde regards with fondness. Their relationship is a friendly connection between the elderly woman and the imaginative youth.
